family: Amendments of the Civil Service Rules and related class orders (X1 type cs_rules_amendment), 1872-1936

mechanisms.description: An order whose only operative content amends the text of the Civil Service Rules, a schedule, or another order or presidential regulation performs its act when issued; under the owner rule it is spent on issue as a command, and the text it inserted lives on only as part of the amended instrument.
An order whose only operative content revokes or rescinds another order is spent on issue.
General revision of 1896 (EO 89) revoked all other civil service rules, ending rule sets prescribed or extended before it.
mechanisms.effective_date_rule: no later than 1896-05-06 (approval date of EO 89); the member may have ended earlier

mechanisms.description: General revision of 1903 (EO 209) replaced the rules of May 6, 1896 and their amendments.

EO 7915 restated the numbered Civil Service Rules in full and EO 8043 restated Schedules A and B in full, both effective 1939-02-01, so no text of the 1903 rules or of any 1903-1938 amendment remained operative as such after that date.
mechanisms.effective_date_rule: 1939-02-01 (effective dates stated in EO 7915 and EO 8043)

mechanisms.description: A named later order revoked, rescinded or superseded the member.

Later restatements (EO 9830 effective 1947-05-01; EO 10577 effective 1955-01-23; OPM regulations in 5 CFR parts 1-10 and 213) carry the Civil Service Rules and excepted-position schedules to the present; where a present provision matches an old one in substance, it rests on these later instruments.

sources.citation: Executive Order 89 (Civil Service Rules), approved May 6, 1896; printed in Richardson, A Compilation of the Messages and Papers of the Presidents, vol. IX, pp. 701-711 (GPO 1898)
sources.title: Civil Service Rules revised and codified, 1896
sources.pin: the President hereby makes and promulgates the following rules and revokes all others
sources.establishes: The 1896 rules revoked every other civil service rule then standing, on their approval date, May 6, 1896 ('Approved , May 6 , 1896').

sources.citation: Executive Order 209 (Civil Service Rules), March 20, 1903, effective April 15, 1903; Wikisource transcription (revision 13537757); printed in the 20th Report of the U.S. Civil Service Commission (FY1903)
sources.title: Civil Service Rules prescribed in lieu of the rules of May 6, 1896
sources.pin: the President promulgates the following rules in lieu of those promulgated May 6, 1896, and the amendments thereof
sources.establishes: The 1903 rules replaced the 1896 rules and their amendments, effective April 15, 1903 ('Approved, to take effect on and after April 15, 1903.'). Held only as a mirror transcription; the official print is to be acquired.

sources.citation: Executive Order 7915, June 24, 1938, Amendment of Civil Service Rules, 3 FR 1519 (June 28, 1938)
sources.title: Civil Service Rules amended to read as follows, effective February 1, 1939
sources.pin: the Civil Service Rules are hereby amended, effective February 1, 1939, to read as follows
sources.establishes: The whole text of the numbered Civil Service Rules was replaced on February 1, 1939; Rule II sec. 3(a) kept Schedules A and B ('Schedules A and B of the civil service rules are continued as a part of the said rules as amended by this order'). Pins quoted with OCR line breaks collapsed.

sources.citation: Executive Order 8043, January 31, 1939, Amending Schedules A and B of the Civil Service Rules, 4 FR 493 (February 2, 1939)
sources.title: Schedules A and B amended to read as follows, effective February 1, 1939
sources.pin: Schedules A and B of the Civil Service Rules are hereby amended to read as follows
sources.establishes: The whole text of Schedules A and B was replaced on February 1, 1939 ('This order shall be effective February 1, 1939.', printed immediately before '[No. 8043]').

sources.citation: Executive Order 9830, February 24, 1947, Amending the Civil Service Rules and Providing for Federal Personnel Administration, 12 FR 1259 (February 25, 1947)
sources.title: Civil Service Rules amended to read as follows, effective May 1, 1947; EO 7915 revoked
sources.establishes: Effective May 1, 1947 the rules were again restated in full (Part II, 'The Civil Service Rules are herebV amended to read as follows' in the OCR) with Schedules A and B set out in sec. 6.4, and Part III revoked EO 7915 by name.

sources.citation: Executive Order 10577, November 22, 1954, Amending the Civil Service Rules and Authorizing a New Appointment System for the Competitive Service, 19 FR 7521 (November 23, 1954)
sources.title: Civil Service Rules amended to read as follows; schedules kept by the Commission
sources.pin: Section 101. The Civil Service Rules are hereby amended to read as follows
sources.establishes: The present Civil Service Rules descend from this restatement; sec. 6.2 makes Schedules A, B and C lists kept by the Commission, and sec. 301 carries the 1947 schedule entries forward only 'unless and until they are removed therefrom by the Commission'.

sources.citation: Executive Order 250, February 5, 1904, Revoking Special Civil Service Rule of July 3, 1902; Wikisource transcription (1904 CSR 79)
sources.title: Revocation of the special rule of July 3, 1902 (EO 179)
sources.pin: The special rule of July 3, 1902, rendering certain persons who were in the employ of the United States in the military government of Cuba
sources.establishes: EO 179 (the special rule of July 3, 1902) was revoked on February 5, 1904; the revocation also shows that a special rule of 1902 was treated as surviving the 1903 general revision.

sources.citation: Executive Order 3014, November 30, 1918; printed in the 36th Report of the U.S. Civil Service Commission (FY1919), p. 104 (CSC report slice)
sources.title: Rescission of the order of October 28, 1918 (EO 2985)
sources.pin: The Executive order of October 28, 1918, authorizing the Civil Service Commis- sion, as a war measure
sources.establishes: EO 2985 (October 28, 1918) was rescinded on November 30, 1918 ('is hereby rescinded').

sources.citation: Executive Order 5459, October 4, 1930, Placing the Position of Shipping Commissioner in the Classified Service (American Presidency Project transcription; 1930 CSR 57)
sources.title: Shipping commissioners classified; EO 3807 superseded
sources.pin: This order supersedes Executive Order No. 3807 of March 15, 1923.

sources.citation: 5 CFR 213.3102 (eCFR as of 2026-11-04), Schedule A, entire executive civil service; [47 FR 28902, July 2, 1982]
sources.title: Current Schedule A, entire executive civil service
sources.establishes: Present Schedule A exceptions rest on OPM regulations republished in 1982 under statute and EO 12364, not on any 1872-1936 order; an exception surviving in substance today is continuity under later instruments.

sources.citation: Bear Lake & River Water Works & Irrigation Co. v. Garland, 164 U.S. 1, 12 (1896)
sources.title: Re-enacted provisions construed as a continuation of the old
sources.pin: should be construed as a continuation of the old with the modification contained in the new act
sources.establishes: Caveat only: provisions re-enacted in a replacing instrument may be read as continued; relevant to whether EO 209 text carried into the 1939 restatement survived, not to the amending orders, which are spent on issue.

procedure.description: EO 89, the 1896 general revision of the Civil Service Rules.

lead.basis: EO 209 (March 20, 1903) promulgated new rules 'in lieu of those promulgated May 6, 1896, and the amendments thereof', effective April 15, 1903.

date_rule.basis: EO 209: 'Approved, to take effect on and after April 15, 1903.'

gaps: EO 209 is held only as a Wikisource mirror transcription; the official print in the FY1903 Civil Service Commission report is to be acquired

procedure.description: EO 209, the 1903 general revision of the Civil Service Rules (rules and Schedule A).

lead.basis: EO 7915 amended the Civil Service Rules 'to read as follows', effective February 1, 1939, keeping the schedules only until EO 8043 amended Schedules A and B 'to read as follows', also effective February 1, 1939; no text of the 1903 instrument remained operative as its own after that date.

date_rule.basis: EO 7915 and EO 8043 stated effective dates

gaps: provisions of 1903 that EO 7915 or EO 8043 repeated word for word could be read as continued rather than ended (Bear Lake v. Garland, 164 U.S. 1, 12); the continuation would rest on EO 7915/8043 and later restatements, and EO 9830 revoked EO 7915 by name; the owner should confirm that re-enactment in a full restatement ends the earlier instrument for the census

gaps: EO 250 is held as a Wikisource mirror transcription

gaps: EO 3014 is held as a Civil Service Commission report slice, not the signed original

procedure.description: No date or no readable summary: cannot be placed in a period.

lead.basis: The member has no date or no summary; its text is an unread scan, so what it does is unknown.

gaps: read the scan (ProQuest page) and retype the member

procedure.description: Special rules of 1897-1902 promulgated as freestanding rules (not amendments of a numbered rule).

lead.basis: A special rule is a freestanding rule. EO 209 replaced the 1896 rules 'and the amendments thereof', but EO 250 revoked a 1902 special rule in 1904, which shows special rules were treated as outlasting the 1903 revision; whether and when each ended is not established.

gaps: for each special rule: its own terms (many except only 'the successor to the present incumbent' and were exhausted on one appointment), and any later revocation; Civil Service Commission reports FY1897-FY1905

procedure.description: Classification orders under section 6 of the Civil Service Act (heads directed to amend their classifications), even where the WPA calls them rule amendments.

when.text_regex: third para-? ?graph of sec|para-? ?graph of section 6 of the act|direct(ed)? .{0,60}to amend (their (several )?classi-? ?fications|the classi-? ?fication)

lead.basis: The order directs department heads to classify a group of positions under section 6 of the 1883 Act; its effect (positions classified) is a continuing state, and no held instrument is shown to have ended it. Later rules saved status so granted (EO 7915 Rule II sec. 1), which is not an end.

gaps: evidence that the positions were later excepted, abolished or reorganized, or a doctrine for covering-in orders (owner decision)

procedure.description: Rule sets prescribed, extended or approved before the 1896 revision (Grant-era rules of 1872-1874; Internal Revenue and Government Printing Office rules of 1895).

lead.basis: EO 89 (May 6, 1896) promulgated the codified rules 'and revokes all others'; any rule set, extension or classification regulation still standing then ended no later than that day.

date_rule.basis: EO 89 approved May 6, 1896; the member may have ended earlier (the Grant-era rules lapsed in practice after 1875; not relied on)

gaps: EO 15 and EO 17 texts are unread scans and this branch relies on their WPA summaries and the Richardson notice for EO 17
EO 89 is held as Richardson's printed compilation, not the signed original

procedure.description: Pure revocations of another order or special rule.

lead.basis: The order's only operative content revokes another order; it is spent on issue as a command, and its effect is evidence for the revoked order's lifecycle.

procedure.description: Waivers, suspensions or exemptions of the rules (not amendments of their text).

lead.basis: The order waives or suspends a rule for a person, group or occasion rather than changing the rule's text; it does not merge into the rules, so the replacement of the rules' text does not by itself end it.

gaps: route to the one-person waiver doctrine (PD-CS-ONE-PERSON) or a class-waiver rule; own terms and use

procedure.description: Amendments of the pre-1896 rule sets (General, Departmental, Customs, Postal, Indian, Internal Revenue, GPO rules and their special rules).

when.text_regex: amend|strik(e|es|ing) out|struck|insert|addition of|adding|to read as follows|hereby revoked|is revoked|eliminat|transfer(red)? .{0,40}(from|to) (subdivision|paragraph)|renumber

lead.basis: The order only amends the text of the civil service rules then in force; it is spent on issue as a command. The text it inserted ended no later than May 6, 1896, when EO 89 'revokes all others'.

gaps: the branch reads the WPA 1944 summary for what the order does and checks the held order text only for amending language; a compiled transcription can run into a neighbouring order
the machine does not confirm that the order contains nothing besides the amendment

procedure.description: Other orders before May 6, 1896 that the WPA summary describes as amending the civil service rules, whose held text does not confirm a pure amendment (empty text, replacement rule, or extra provisions).

not.text_regex: third para-? ?graph of sec|para-? ?graph of section 6 of the act|direct(ed)? .{0,60}to amend (their (several )?classi-? ?fications|the classi-? ?fication)

lead.basis: Whatever the order did to the civil service rules then in force, EO 89 (May 6, 1896) promulgated the codified rules 'and revokes all others', so any rule text or rule the order made ended no later than that day.

gaps: the held text does not confirm what the order did; the branch relies on the WPA summary that it acted on the civil service rules
EO 89 is held as Richardson's printed compilation

procedure.description: Amendments of the 1896 rules (May 6, 1896 to April 14, 1903).

lead.basis: The order only amends the text of the 1896 Civil Service Rules (EO 89); it is spent on issue as a command. The text it inserted ended no later than April 15, 1903, when EO 209 took effect 'in lieu of those promulgated May 6, 1896, and the amendments thereof'.

gaps: the branch reads the WPA 1944 summary for what the order does and checks the held order text only for amending language; a compiled transcription can run into a neighbouring order
the machine does not confirm that the order contains nothing besides the amendment
EO 209 held only as a mirror transcription

procedure.description: Amendments of the 1903 rules or of Schedules A and B (April 15, 1903 to 1938).

when.text_regex: amend|strik(e|es|ing) out|struck|insert|addition of|adding|to read as follows|hereby revoked|is revoked|eliminat|transfer(red)? .{0,40}(from|to) (subdivision|paragraph)|renumber

lead.basis: The order only amends the text of a numbered Civil Service Rule or of Schedule A or B of the 1903 rules (EO 209); it is spent on issue as a command. The text it inserted ended no later than February 1, 1939, when EO 7915 (rules) and EO 8043 (Schedules A and B) restated that text in full; any same-substance provision today rests on later instruments (EO 9830, EO 10577, 5 CFR).

gaps: the branch reads the WPA 1944 summary for what the order does and checks the held order text only for amending language; a compiled transcription can run into a neighbouring order
the machine does not confirm that the order contains nothing besides the amendment

procedure.description: Pure amendments of another executive order or of presidential personnel regulations (labor regulations, postmaster regulations, Diplomatic Service regulations).

when.text_regex: amend|strik(e|es|ing) out|struck|insert|addition of|adding|to read as follows|hereby revoked|is revoked|eliminat|transfer(red)? .{0,40}(from|to) (subdivision|paragraph)|renumber

lead.basis: The order's only operative content amends another executive order or a set of regulations the President prescribed; it is spent on issue as a command, and its effect is evidence for the amended instrument's lifecycle.

gaps: the branch reads the WPA 1944 summary for what the order does and checks the held order text only for amending language; a compiled transcription can run into a neighbouring order
the machine does not confirm that the order contains nothing besides the amendment

procedure.description: Class orders: positions or groups classified, covered into or placed outside the classified service, or excepted, by standalone order.

when.summary_regex: classif(y|ied|ication)|covered into|competitive classified|placed (with|in|within|outside|under)|unclassified service|outside (of )?the classified|excepted from (examination|civil service)|exempted from|included .{0,60}(in|within) the (competitive )?classified|granted all rights

lead.basis: The order places a group of positions (sometimes with their incumbents) in or out of the classified service, or excepts them, without amending the rules' text; its effect is a continuing state that the 1939 and later restatements did not end by their terms (EO 7915 Rule II sec. 1 saves status granted by such orders).

gaps: later exception, abolition, reorganization or revocation of the positions concerned; owner decision on covering-in orders

procedure.description: Other presidential personnel regulations prescribed (labor, postmaster, efficiency rating, reduction in force, furlough, diplomatic service).

lead.basis: The order prescribes a separate body of regulations, not part of the Civil Service Rules; the rules' restatements do not reach it by their terms.

gaps: the later order that replaced each regulation set (e.g., successive postmaster regulations of 1917, 1926, 1929, 1936; labor regulations) and its revocation clause

procedure.description: Summary describes an amendment of the rules, a schedule or another order, but either the summary shows further provisions (prescribed, construed) or the held text does not show amending language (wrong, empty or unreadable text).

lead.basis: The WPA summary calls the order an amendment, but the held text does not confirm it (the text is empty, an unread scan, a restated regulation without amending words, or a neighbouring order).

gaps: a correct text of the order (Civil Service Commission annual report for the year cited in the WPA entry, or the State Department/National Archives copy); once confirmed, the member falls into B12-B15

procedure.description: EO 5514: departments in the District of Columbia closed on December 24, 1930 (a closing order typed into this family).

lead.basis: The order closed the departments and excused employees on one stated day, December 24, 1930, and 'is not to be deemed as establishing a precedent'.

date_rule.basis: the day stated in the order

gaps: order text is an American Presidency Project transcription; the member belongs to the closing family (TR-CLOSING-MOURNING)

procedure.description: EO 5977: departments in the District of Columbia closed on December 24 and 31, 1932 (a closing order typed into this family).

lead.basis: The order closed the departments and excused employees on two stated days, the later being December 31, 1932.

date_rule.basis: the later day stated in the order

gaps: the member belongs to the closing family (TR-CLOSING-MOURNING)

procedure.description: Catch-all: other orders typed into this family (directives, transfers of functions, closings, one-person orders).

lead.basis: The order is not an amendment of the Civil Service Rules or a class order; no mechanism of this doctrine applies.

gaps: retype the member and apply the doctrine for its true type

undecidable.reason: special rules of 1897-1902 promulgated as freestanding rules; EO 250 shows special rules were treated as outliving the 1903 revision, so EO 209 does not end them by its terms

classification and covering-in orders (section 6 classifications, positions classified, covered in, placed outside the classified service or excepted by standalone order): continuing effect, saved by later rules, no ending instrument shown
waivers and suspensions of a rule for a person, group or occasion: not merged into the rules' text; belong to the waiver doctrines

separate presidential regulation sets (labor, postmaster, efficiency rating, reduction in force, furlough, diplomatic service): the rules' restatements do not reach them; successor regulations not yet traced
summary says amendment but the held text is empty, a scan, the wrong order, a restatement without amending words, or shows further provisions
no date or no summary, unread scan
orders of other types typed into this family (directives, transfers of functions or records, one-person orders, Boxer indemnity, seals)
